title: Introduce subnet label-driven peering and DNS policy engine
author: Ananya Rao
description: Motivation: Provide an idempotent, label-driven reconciliation engine that automates VPC peering, subnet ownership assignments, conditional security group attachments, and Route53 private DNS policy wiring for control plane private deployments. Many installers required manual peering and ad-hoc route updates during multi-account and multi-AZ rollouts; this PR introduces a declarative label surface (subnet:role=controlplane|egress|workload and subnet:owner=region/zone/team) and a controller that creates deterministic peering attachments, route propagation, and DNS forwarding records with safe rollback hooks. High-level changes: 1) Terraform module updates to network module to accept subnet labels and to expose peering resource metadata for external controllers; 2) New lightweight reconciler binary (installer/reconciler) that reads desired subnet labels from TF state or cluster config and performs peering/route53 actions via AWS APIs with exponential backoff and state checkpoints; 3) Helm chart changes to controlplane to add DNS glue environment and a readiness probe that verifies private-hosted-zone delegation before advertising endpoints; 4) Upgrade/rollback tooling: terraform plan integration with --dry-run reconciliation mode, a staged canary rollout for peering attachments, and a 'peering-safeclean' command that performs non-destructive teardown and verifies route/classic-record removal; 5) Acceptance and e2e smoke tests that simulate cross-account peering and conditional sg injection. The description below summarizes design, commits, files touched, testing, rollout and rollback instructions, and outstanding follow-ups. Checklist: [x] Add subnet label TF variables and outputs [x] Implement reconciler CLI + unit tests [x] Helm chart: add dnsGlue config + probe [x] Add smoke/e2e tests in perf-canary harness [x] Document runbook and rollback steps [x] CI passing on integration runner. Commits summary: feat(tf): add subnet labels and peering metadata outputs; feat(reconciler): initial controller + checkpointing; fix(reconciler): backoff & idempotency on duplicate attachments; feat(helm): dns-glue env + readiness probe; test(e2e): add cross-account peering smoke; docs: runbook and upgrade notes. Files changed (high level): installer/terraform/modules/network/variables.tf, installer/terraform/modules/network/outputs.tf, installer/terraform/modules/network/peering.tf, installer/reconciler/main.go, installer/reconciler/checkpoint.go, installer/reconciler/aws_client.go, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/values.yaml, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/templates/dns-glue-configmap.yaml, installer/helm/charts/controlplane/templates/readiness-probe.yaml, tests/perf-canary/e2e/peering_smoke_test.go, docs/runbooks/private-controlplane-peering.md, scripts/peering-safeclean.sh, ci/integration/reconciler_integration.yml. Testing performed: unit tests for reconciler (covering duplicate-peering, transient API failures), integration job against a long-running dev AWS account (peering create/accept/route-sync), Helm chart acceptance where readiness probe blocks traffic until DNS glue is present, and an e2e smoke that validated Route53 resolver rules in a shared-hosted-zone configuration. Rollout plan: 1) Deploy TF changes with --target module.network and capture outputs; 2) Run reconciler in --dry-run mode to assert intended peering actions; 3) Rollout reconciler as pre-deploy job to create peering attachments; 4) Deploy controlplane Helm chart (first canary AZ, then global) and validate readiness; 5) Promote reconciler to 'managed' mode to perform route and DNS record updates. Rollback plan: reconciler supports --reconcile-mode=dry|apply|revert; to revert, run --reconcile-mode=revert which performs non-destructive withdrawal of routes and peering attachments while preserving checkpoints to avoid accidently removing shared resources. Security notes: peers are created with restricted security groups and a deterministic tag format (redwood:peering=<cluster>-<env>) so automated cleanup and billing attribution works. Migration notes: Existing installs without subnet labels are supported via a discovery mode (reconciler infers role by CIDR -> az mapping) but will log a migration suggestion to add labels. Outstanding follow-ups: add GCP/Azure provider adapters (tracked ENG-1903), expand RBAC around reconciler KMS usage, and add more granular CircuitBreaker controls in the reconciler to avoid mass-peering during region faults. Merge rationale: validated in integration, adds safe rollback paths and non-breaking terraform outputs; decided to squash merge to keep tf history compact.

feat(reconciler): initial implementation of label-driven reconciler with checkpointing
fix(reconciler): handle duplicate peering create errors and add retry/backoff
feat(helm): add dnsGlue and readiness probe to controlplane chart

review_comments: Marcus Liu: Can the reconciler avoid creating peering across accounts that are in a billing relationship edge-case? Please add a guard and a dry-run abort on suspicious cross-account pairings.
Author (Ananya Rao): Added a preflight guard that checks allowed-account-list, and reconciler now emits a high-severity log and requires --force to proceed if accounts are not in allowlist.
Helen Park: Helm readiness probe looks good, but add a tolerance for eventual DNS propagation delays (60s -> 300s).
Author (Ananya Rao): Increased probe timeout to 300s and added a toggleable environment variable 'DNS_PROBE_TIMEOUT' to values.yaml.
release_notes: Add label-driven subnet peering automation and DNS policy engine. Terraform exposes new subnet label inputs and peering metadata outputs. New reconciler binary performs idempotent peering, route and private-hosted-zone wiring with dry-run and revert modes. Helm controlplane chart gets DNS glue and readiness probe. Rollback-safe with 'revert' reconcile mode and peering-safeclean helper.
